findings.title: Database writes and ZADD queue:priority:<tier> can get out of step
findings.consequence: `INSERT jobs`, `UPDATE jobs SET status='pending', attempts by id + status` and `UPDATE jobs SET status='pending', error by id` each commit first, then Redis is updated in a separate call. If Redis is down or the process dies in between, the two disagree: the row says one thing, Redis another, and nothing repairs it later. The caller may also get an error for work that was in fact saved.
findings.fix: Make the database the source of truth and rebuild Redis from it: write an outbox row in the same transaction and let a worker update Redis, or run a periodic job that re-syncs Redis from the database.

findings.title: COUNT jobs per status scans all of jobs on every call
findings.consequence: Counting or summing with no WHERE reads every row of jobs each time. It's quick while the table is small and grows linearly with it, and every caller pays it.
findings.fix: Keep running counters (update them when rows change), cache the result for a few seconds, or restrict the query with a WHERE on an indexed column.

findings.title: Every open tab polls GET /stats every 5 s on top of its live WebSocket
findings.consequence: The browser asks whether anything changed even when nothing did. 10,000 open tabs make about 2,000 requests per second to GET /stats, most returning the same data. Cost grows with users, not with how often data changes. This page already receives pushed updates, so the timer mostly repeats work.
findings.fix: Send what GET /stats returns over the socket (or push a snapshot every few seconds from the server). If the timer also catches things the socket can't report, keep it but slow it down.

findings.title: Each pushed message makes every browser call GET /stats
findings.consequence: The server pushes an event and every connected page answers by requesting GET /stats. 100 open dashboards and 20 events per second become 2,000 requests per second to GET /stats, more load than polling would cause.
findings.fix: Send the data the page needs inside the pushed message, refresh only for the message types that change it, or debounce the refresh.

findings.title: Redis call inside a loop in queueService.claimNextJob
findings.consequence: The loop sends `ZRANGEBYSCORE queue:priority:<tier>` on each pass and stops at the first hit. When something is found early that's one or two round trips; when nothing matches, it makes one per pass, every time.
findings.fix: Send the commands in one round trip: a pipeline (or MULTI), MGET for plain keys, or restructure so one command answers the question.

findings.title: idx_jobs_status duplicates idx_jobs_status_priority_run_at on jobs
findings.consequence: idx_jobs_status_priority_run_at starts with the same columns, so one of the two never helps a read. Every insert and update still maintains both, which costs write time and disk. No query here filters or sorts on priority and run_at, so the longer index is the one doing no work.
findings.fix: Keep idx_jobs_status and drop idx_jobs_status_priority_run_at in a new migration (DROP INDEX IF EXISTS idx_jobs_status_priority_run_at;). If your migration runner re-applies every file, also remove the CREATE INDEX for it, or it comes back.

findings.title: SELECT jobs by status, page (LIMIT/OFFSET) sorts without a matching index
findings.consequence: No index hands rows out in id order within status, so to return the first page the database may have to collect every matching row of jobs and sort them before the LIMIT applies. Then each page costs as much as reading all of them.
findings.fix: Add an index on the filter columns followed by the sort columns, in a new migration: CREATE INDEX ON jobs (status, id);

findings.title: Worker checks Redis for work every 1 s even when there is none
findings.consequence: An idle worker keeps asking Redis whether there's work, and a new job waits up to 1 s before a worker notices it. Each extra idle worker adds the same steady trickle of empty reads.
findings.fix: Wake idle workers when work arrives (a pub/sub message, LISTEN/NOTIFY, or a blocking pop where the data structure allows it) and keep a slower timer as a fallback for delayed jobs.
